accuracy.evidence: Matches KS1 living-things contexts: wild (self-sufficient, observe), farm (kept for products), pet (companionship + daily care).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets grab-a-fox, every-animal-is-a-pet, farm=wild self-care, and pets-need-no-people in why() and adult notes.

lab_distinct.evidence: Lab sorts care groups and safe-distance rules — distinct from habitat homes (flaghome) and alive/not-alive sorting (flagalive).

lab_teaches.evidence: Learner sorts fox to wild, picks self-feeding vs pet care, chooses watch-not-touch, places sheep as farm.

predictions.evidence: Wrong options (house pet fox, grab cuddle, never need people) are overturned by sort/food/distance/petcare tasks.

challenge_feedback.evidence: why() names house/cuddles/grab/secret, wool/pen/farmdef, nocare/never/hunt, science/forbid slips specifically.

readability.evidence: Ages 5–7 wording: short kid lines; wild, farm, pet, safe distance named plainly.

no_filler.evidence: No delve/journey phrasing; each line teaches a care group or a safety rule to keep.

mobile.evidence: Large sort/distance buttons; tap twins for drag; challenge stack usable at phone width; young class.

accessibility.evidence: Sort, food, distance, petcare, mixup, idea expose lbtn twins; say() updates canvas aria-label; challenge uses aria-live status.

sources: UK National Curriculum Science KS1: animals, including humans — identify and name common animals; habitats care contexts
RSPCA / wildlife education: observe wild animals; do not approach or feed as pets
BBC Bitesize KS1 Science: animals — pets, farm animals and wild animals
